text: Justice Stephen Breyer wrote the opinion. A school's authority over what students say, he explained, is weaker off campus than on. There, a student is in the care of her parents.

text: Then came the line the ruling turns on. America's public schools, he wrote, are the nurseries of democracy. The place a free society teaches the next generation to tolerate the speech it dislikes. A school that punishes every unpopular word teaches the opposite.

text: The 1969 Tinker rule lets a school discipline speech that substantially disrupts it. A few minutes of talk does not.
provenance: But a school can discipline speech that would "substantially disrupt" the school — that genuinely interferes with running it.
